sources.title: A two process model of sleep regulation
sources.note: Foundational two-process model (Process S + Process C); historical 1982 paper, predates PMC digitization

sources.authors: Porkka-Heiskanen T, Strecker RE, Thakkar M, Bjorkum AA, Greene RW, McCarley RW
sources.title: Adenosine: a mediator of the sleep-inducing effects of prolonged wakefulness
sources.note: Direct evidence of adenosine accumulation in basal forebrain during wakefulness; adenosine transport inhibitor mimics sleep deprivation recovery

sources.authors: Halassa MM, Florian C, Fellin T, Munoz JR, Lee SY, Abel T, Haydon PG, Frank MG
sources.title: Astrocytic modulation of sleep homeostasis and cognitive consequences of sleep loss
sources.note: DNSNARE transgenic mice; blocking astrocytic gliotransmission attenuates SWA rebound; rescued by exogenous adenosine

sources.authors: Bjorness TE, Kelly CL, Gao T, Poffenberger V, Greene RW
sources.title: Control and function of the homeostatic sleep response by adenosine A1 receptors
sources.note: Conditional A1R knockout abolishes SWA rebound; working memory impaired during sleep restriction in A1R-cKO

sources.authors: Lazarus M, Oishi Y, Bjorness TE, Greene RW
sources.title: Gating and the Need for Sleep: Dissociable Effects of Adenosine A1 and A2A Receptors
sources.note: Framework paper: A1R (homeostatic SWA depth, BF) vs A2A (sleep gating, NAc/ventral striatum); caffeine blocks both

sources.journal: Neurobiology of Sleep and Circadian Rhythms
sources.title: Sleep homeostasis and the circadian clock: Do the circadian pacemaker and the sleep homeostat influence each other's functioning?
sources.note: Process S and Process C bidirectional interaction; strong circadian function promotes deep NREM; high sleep pressure reduces light-responsiveness

sources.authors: Bellier F, Walter A, Lecoin L, Chauveau F, Rouach N, Rancillac A
sources.title: Astrocytes at the heart of sleep: from genes to network dynamics
sources.note: 2025 comprehensive review: astrocyte Ca2+ dynamics, gap junctions, gliotransmission in sleep-wake regulation; most current overview

sources.title: Methylxanthines and sleep
sources.note: Caffeine mechanism: non-selective competitive antagonism of adenosine A1/A2A receptors; individual sensitivity via ADORA2A polymorphism

sources.authors: Gass N, Porkka-Heiskanen T, Kalinchuk AV
sources.title: The role of the basal forebrain adenosine receptors in sleep homeostasis
sources.note: Intracerebral adenosine receptor antagonism: BF A1R block reduces recovery sleep/SWA; A2AR block no effect → BF A1R mediates homeostatic recovery
